cameras.name: Steel Information Center
cameras.description: The Steel Information Center at Park Headquarters (elevation 6,450 feet) is open daily except December 25th. This view is useful in showing the amount of snow currently on the ground in the park. It can be 10 to 15 feet deep in the late winter and early spring.

cameras.name: Bald Hills & Redwood Creek
cameras.description: This view from the Schoolhouse Peak Lookout located in the Bald Hills is oriented to the west, across a portion of open prairie in the middle distance to the Redwood Creek watershed beyond it. This diverse landscape composed of grasslands and oak woodlands provides optimal habitat for bird species that are rarely seen elsewhere in Redwood National and State Parks, including reintroduced California

cameras.name: Annie Spring Entrance Station
cameras.description: Curious about road conditions? This webcam can help you determine if the park's roads are icy. It looks south along Munson Valley Road from the Annie Spring Entrance Station (elevation 6,000 feet). The silver bar is a flagpole.

cameras.name: Bright Angel Trailhead View
cameras.description: Verify that the time and date of the picture is current (upper right in the photo). IMPORTANT: At this time, the Bright Angel Trail is open to the River Resthouse. The River Trail east of the River Resthouse to the South Kaibab Trail junction and the Silver Bridge remain closed through June 30, 2026. (Reason: waterline construction).

cameras.name: Dorchester Heights Monument - Looking South
cameras.description: This view primarily shows the cove forming Carson Beach as well as the open fields of Moakley Park. Beyond on the other side of the cove is the campus of UMass Boston and the JFK Presidential Library. The Dorchester neighborhood lies beyond. In the near field below are a number of multi-family residences featuring a variety of architectural styles, as well as more modern apartment complexes.

cameras.name: Dorchester Heights Monument - Looking North
cameras.description: This camera looks out over the city skyline of downtown Boston in the distance. In the midground is the Seaport neighborhood, dominated by the large Boston Convention and Exposition Center. Closer in are the many multi-family buildings that define South Boston. Many are wood painted different colors, others are brick. Many feature a variety of architectural features, such as bays and mansard roofs

cameras.name: Dorchester Heights Monument - Looking East
cameras.description: The dominant feature in the near-field in this view is the back of the beige-brick South Boston High School building. It has a pitched center roof in the center with a weathered green patina. Wings of the school stretch to the left and right. cameras.description: Is Crater Lake visible today? Sometimes the lake is hidden by clouds, especially in the winter. This view looks north across the lake from the Sinnott Overlook at Rim Village (elevation 7,100 feet). On a clear day, it takes in Wizard Island, Llao Rock, and Mount Thielsen. cameras.name: El Capitan View
cameras.description: View from the Pine Springs area towards the southwest and the profile of El Capitan - "View Webcam" link opens a larger picture that updates every 30 seconds.

cameras.description: Alpine Visitor Center, located at the top of Fall River Pass, is at an elevation of 11,796 feet above sea level. cameras.name: Kawuneeche Valley
cameras.description: Located on the west side of Rocky Mountain National Park, the Kawuneeche Valley is home to a variety of flora and fauna. This webcam shows views of Harbison Meadow, located 0.5-miles north of the Grand Lake Entrance. Enjoy views of the Never Summer Mountains in the distance.

cameras.name: Continental Divide
cameras.description: The Continental Divide Webcam offers a spectacular view of a meadow near Glacier Basin Campground and stunning mountain peaks in the distance. On a clear day, enjoy views of Thatchtop, Taylor Peak, Otis Peak, Hallett Peak, and Flattop Mountain.

cameras.name: Longs Peak
cameras.description: Longs Peak towers over all other peaks in Rocky Mountain National Park at an elevation of 14,259 feet above sea level. It is a challenging mountain to climb under the best conditions. This webcam shows views of Longs Peak as seen from the Tahosa Valley.

cameras.name: Fall River Entrance/U.S. Hwy 34
cameras.description: Fall River Entrance is located just west of the Town of Estes Park on U.S. Highway 34. This view is looking east from the entrance station, depicting the flow of vehicles entering the park.

cameras.name: Beaver Meadows Entrance/U.S. Hwy 36

cameras.name: Mount Washburn - Northeastern View
cameras.description: At 10,219 feet, Mount Washburn towers above Dunraven Pass between Tower Junction and Canyon Village. A fire lookout stationed at the summit provides a popular destination for day hikers, as well as housing for an employee who watches for and tracks fires throughout the summer. This webcam is located inside the living quarters on the top floor and looks out to the northeast.

cameras.name: North Entrance - Electric Peak
cameras.description: Morning views from this webcam are spectacular, especially during the winter when the morning sun touches Electric Peak. Look for wildlife—elk, bison, and pronghorn can be seen grazing here. Occasionally you may see the top of oversize vehicles—RVs, tour buses, and delivery trucks—as they stop at the entrance station.

cameras.name: North Entrance - Out of the Park
cameras.description: This webcam is on the park's North Entrance at Gardiner, Montana. It shows current conditions at the entrance with Roosevelt Arch in the background. cameras.name: West Entrance - Out of the Park

cameras.name: Apgar Village

Originally it was only going to be a test until a better location was found, but it turns out that this view has a large following. Watch for the occasional lunchtime crowd at the picnic table or our resident deer wandering about. Some years in the early summer beargrass blooms dot the forest.

cameras.name: Carlsbad Caverns Natural Entrance Camera
cameras.description: Perched above the natural entrance this camera shows the mouth of the cave and the winding trail that descends into the cavern. It's also where the bats emerge from each night. Carlsbad Cavern is one of the most famous and venerated caves on Earth. It is also home to several hundred thousand Brazilian free-tailed bats.
